sources.title: Florida Department of Children and Families, Office of Inspector General — Appeal Hearings
sources.notes: The standing packet says this host 'refuses or defeats plain curl' and was captured through a session fetch tool; retested 2026-09-03, plain curl with a browser user-agent now returns 200 with the full page, including the hearing office's address (2415 North Monroe Street), phone (850) 488-1429 and the 'individual or family“s eligibility' string the standing packet quotes verbatim. Whatever blocked it on 2026-08-30 no longer does, or never did with this header. The page's own <main id="main-content"> element is empty in the served markup — the card content the page displays sits directly in <body>, several containers below main — so 'body' is the narrowest scope that is honestly stated and complete; it is also a superset of the standing packet's hand-curated excerpt, which the recipe README treats as safe.

sources.title: Florida Administrative Code Chapter 65-2, Rules of Practice and Procedure (Department of Children and Families)
sources.source_date: most sections effective 4/2/2018 (per each rule's own History line on flrules.org; 65-2.058 effective 12/11/2006 and 65-2.060 effective 10/30/2000 are not amended by the 2018 rulemaking)
sources.notes: Captured to resolve the department's fair-hearing procedural rule that s. 400.0255(15)(b) points to ('equivalent to the procedures used for fair hearings for other Medicaid cases, chapter 10-2, part VI, Florida Administrative Code'): each rule in the current chapter carries a History line reading 'Formerly 10-2.xx, 10-2.0xx', so chapter 65-2 is chapter 10-2 under its current number, though the current chapter prints no 'Part' subdivisions and this page cannot confirm which rules made up 'Part VI' specifically -- recorded as a finding, not resolved. flrules.org (Florida's official Administrative Code publisher) serves this chapter's full current text only as a single legacy binary Word file (Composite Document Format / 'Word 6.0/95', per the `file` command), not as a .docx, PDF, or HTML rendering -- checked: the chapter's own listing page offers no other format, and every individual rule's own readFile.asp link is the same legacy .doc format. tools/capture.py's docx extractor is python-docx, which reads only the OOXML .docx container and raises on this file (a compound binary document, not a zip). curl fetches the exact bytes fine (no WAF, no session token, no query hash in the URL -- it is a stable, directly-linked download) but capture.py has no extractor in its closed vocabulary for a legacy binary .doc, so the fetched bytes cannot be turned into text by anything already in the tool. Per this pass's constraint against modifying tools/capture.py, the file was fetched with curl exactly as capture.py's own fetch_curl would fetch it, then converted to plain text outside capture.py with the macOS `textutil -convert txt` utility (not python-docx, and not one of capture.py's own extractors), and handed to capture.py with `--supply 5=<converted file>`. THE EXTRACTOR FIELD ABOVE IS DECLARATIVE ONLY: because the supplied text is a Python str and this source's declared extractor is one of the ones capture.py treats as needing a binary decode, capture.py's own logic (capture_source(), the 'a supplied agent fetch is already text' branch) takes the supplied text as already-extracted and does not attempt to run python-docx on it. The auto-generated annotation on this source elsewhere in these capture notes reads '(fetched by the session reader and supplied)' -- that phrase is capture.py's own fixed wording for any supplied source and is not fully accurate here: the FETCH was plain curl, identical to what capture.py would do unattended; only the DOC-TO-TEXT CONVERSION was performed outside capture.py, because of the missing legacy-.doc extractor. Re-running `python3 tools/capture.py florida` without a fresh --supply for source 5 will fail loudly with a python-docx exception on this file's binary header, not silently reproduce or corrupt this text -- this is a genuine tools/capture.py gap (no extractor for the legacy binary .doc format), reported for the tool to gain one, or for this source to be re-based on an OOXML or PDF republication if flrules.org ever offers one for this chapter.

sources.title: Florida Medicaid Nursing Facility Services Coverage Policy, Rule 59G-4.200, F.A.C. (Agency for Health Care Administration)
sources.notes: Found from ahca.myflorida.com's own 'Adopted Rules and Service Specific Policies' listing page (medicaid/rules/adopted-rules-service-specific-policies.html), which links this PDF as '59G-4.200 Nursing Facility Services Coverage Policy'; the document's own section 1.2 states its legal authority as 'Rule 59G-4.200, F.A.C.' among others. This is AHCA's own first-party statement of the Medicaid bed-hold ('leave days') policy the licensure statute (400.0255(6), 400.022(1)(u)) refers to without stating a Medicaid-specific day count of its own: section 4.2.1, 'Leave Days', states 'Florida Medicaid reimburses for leave days when the recipient is expected to return to the facility, as follows: Hospitalization -- 8 days per medically necessary hospital stay; Therapeutic leave -- 16 days per state fiscal year.' This 8-day figure differs from 400.022(1)(u)'s own 'up to 15 days' for a Title XIX (Medicaid) resident's hospitalization bed reservation; both are quoted on the page as published by their own publishers and are not reconciled. Single-column PDF, seven pages, no WAF encountered; plain curl with a browser user-agent returns 200 directly.
